Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

scopusflow (development version)

Upgrading from the previous release (0.4.0)

Changed results

  • scopus_compare_topics() sends each comparison as (reference) AND (term), where, without field, it joined them without brackets, so a reference with a top-level AND NOT took the term into its negation and shares could pass 100%. Re-run such comparisons made without field. Given field, only the query column differs.
  • scopus_query() brackets each term of several words, other than a quoted or braced phrase or a bracketed or field-tagged group, when it joins terms without .field, so scopus_query("machine learning", "deep learning", .op = "OR") gives (machine learning) OR (deep learning), where ‘Scopus’ read the unbracketed join as machine AND (learning OR deep) AND learning. It also trims each term.
  • Under view = "COMPLETE", the authors column lists every author, up to the API’s 100, as "Surname, Given" joined by "; ", where it held the first author alone. COMPLETE checkpoints from 0.4.0 are fetched again once, each with a scopus_warning_cache_mismatch warning.
  • scopus_abstract(view = "REF", include = "references") and scopus_corpus(view = "REF") return the whole reference list, at one request per 40 references, where they returned about the first 40. The title and source of each reference are read, where both were NA. REF checkpoints from 0.4.0 are fetched again once.
  • scopus_fetch() and scopus_fetch_plan() advance by the records each page returns, where a page shorter than requested made them skip records. STANDARD plan checkpoints from 0.4.0 are served as before, so re-run with resume = FALSE a plan that warned of a shortfall.
  • Requests are retried after a transport failure, such as a timeout or a reset connection, where, under httr2 1.0.4 or later, scopus_abstract() and scopus_corpus() gave the identifier an NA row with a warning and other functions stopped with an error.
  • scopus_combine(dedupe = TRUE) matches DOIs without resolver prefixes and joins a record without a ‘Scopus’ identifier, a blank one included, to the identified record with its DOI, where 0.4.0 kept them apart and merged all records with a blank identifier. dedupe = "id_then_doi" restores the 0.4.0 rule.
  • scopus_abstract() requests view = "META_ABS" by default, where it sent no view, which Elsevier documents as giving no abstract, although the API has returned one. With a key not entitled to that view, the call stops with scopus_error_forbidden (HTTP 403). view = NULL restores the 0.4.0 request and reads its checkpoints.
  • scopus_top(by = "author"), as_bibtex() and as_ris() split an author list at a semicolon with or without a space after it, where a list joined with ";" alone, as version 0.3.0 of the Python twin wrote it, counted as one author.
  • as_bibliometrix() gives AU names as surname and initials joined by ";", such as "ZHANG F;LI X", where it upper-cased the authors string, and UT as the upper-cased EID, where it gave the bare identifier. A set carrying author keywords gains DE.
  • read_scopus_records() reads a .csv file as UTF-8 in every locale and a blank field as NA, where it followed the locale’s encoding and read a blank field as an empty string.
  • The app’s ‘Author’ choice under ‘Search in’ sends AUTH, where it sent AUTHLASTNAME, which searches surnames alone.
  • run_app() leaves its ‘Max records per cell’ field blank, where the field, labelled ‘Max records per year’ in 0.4.0, capped at 200 records each year or, with ‘Partition by year’ off, the whole search. Entering 200 restores that cap.
  • run_app() opens its year slider on 2015 to 2024, where it opened on the last six years.
  • scopus_abstract() and scopus_corpus() give no keyword for a lone author-keyword entry without text, where they gave the keyword "true". Checkpoints from 0.4.0 keep that keyword, so re-run such a batch with resume = FALSE.
  • The app trims the query before every request, so it sends the query the script panel shows, where ‘Check size’, ‘Compare topics’ and ‘Fetch records’ sent it as typed.

Changed interface

  • scopus_plan(), scopus_count(), scopus_fetch(), scopus_trend(), scopus_compare_topics() and scopus_intersections() refuse with scopus_error_bad_input, before any request, unbalanced brackets, quotation marks or braces and the LIMIT-TO() and EXCLUDE() refinements that the Search API ignores, with which a search ran unfiltered.
  • scopus_plan() given field refuses with scopus_error_bad_input a query, and scopus_query() given .field a term, that already opens with a field tag, where they nested the tags, which the API rejects. scopus_count(), scopus_fetch(), scopus_trend() and scopus_compare_topics() refuse such a query before the request.
  • scopus_error_bad_input inherits scopus_error, so a handler for scopus_error catches input errors, and an invalid view, partition, by, .op or style raises it too. A retry loop on scopus_error should not retry this subclass.
  • scopusflow requires httr2 1.0.4 or later, and its app shiny 1.6.0 or later.
  • scopus_corpus() returns a scopus_id column in second place, so code that selects its columns by position needs updating.
  • A logical argument such as cursor, resume, verbose, dedupe in scopus_extract_dois() or create in scopus_cache_dir() must be TRUE or FALSE, where cursor, dedupe and create read "TRUE", 1 and NA as FALSE.
  • scopus_combine() refuses any dedupe but TRUE, FALSE or a rule name, where NA or another value meant no de-duplication.
  • scopus_trend(), scopus_compare_topics() and scopus_plan(partition = "year") refuse an empty years with scopus_error_bad_input, as they refuse years = NULL, where scopus_trend() returned an empty trend, scopus_compare_topics() stopped with an untyped error and scopus_plan() built a plan without cells.
  • scopus_fetch_plan(), scopus_abstract() and scopus_corpus() refuse with scopus_error_bad_input, before any request, a cache_dir in which no file can be created, where 0.4.0 read its checkpoints and lost any records it fetched to an error. Copy a read-only cache to a writable directory.
  • The options scopusflow.base_url and scopusflow.abstract_url accept only an https URL on api.elsevier.com or another host under elsevier.com, so the API key goes to Elsevier alone. Any other value is refused before a request.

Changed output

  • scopus_search_report() dates a harvest from its first retrieval to its last, where it gave the first alone, lists year cells with gaps separately, where it gave one span, names a max_results cap and supplies PRISMA-S item 2.
  • For a set without a plan, scopus_search_report() calls the year limit unrecorded, where it said that no year limit was applied, and leaves PRISMA-S item 8 to the author.
  • scopus_fetch() attaches the plan it ran, so the search record of its result states the field tag and years and gives a reproduction snippet.
  • Given a one-cell plan for a set without per-cell counts, scopus_search_report() reports the set’s own counts, where it called them unrecorded.
  • PRISMA-S item 16 of scopus_search_report() names the de-duplication rule and the number of DOIs that records with different identifiers share, which scopus_combine() records in its combined attribute as rule and doi_conflicts.
  • In demo mode, the app’s search record names no search expression and says that the records were replayed and that it describes no search that was run, where it gave the bundled corpus’s phrase as the search expression.
  • as_bibtex() and as_ris() write a name ending in initials as ‘Surname, I.’, where BibTeX read the initials as the family name and Zotero kept each RIS author as one field. Citation keys are unchanged.
  • as_bibtex() spaces run-together initials, which BibTeX read as one given name, and protects words such as DNA in titles from lower-casing.
  • as_ris() gives the source title as T2 in place of JO and adds DB - Scopus and the EID as AN.
  • as_ris() and as_bibtex() export an authkeywords or abstract column, as a COMPLETE harvest (the abstract with fields = "extended") or scopus_abstract() gives, where they wrote neither.
  • Every file the package writes is UTF-8 in every locale, where a C or single-byte locale wrote a character it could not encode as text such as <U+00ED>.
  • autoplot() of a record set, a scopus_fetch() result included, draws a bar, zero if need be, for each year its plan searched, where its bars ran from the first year in the records to the last.
  • When the max_results cap stopped a cell, autoplot() of a record set says that the bars count retrieved records.
  • When the years plotted reach the year of retrieval, plot_scopus_trend() and autoplot() of a trend or a record set add a caption line saying that it and any later year were incomplete when retrieved. They read the year from retrieved_at, which scopus_trend() also records.
  • scopus_fetch() warns with scopus_warning_shortfall, as plan cells do, when it retrieves fewer records than the API reported, unless max_results or the offset ceiling stopped it.
  • scopus_plan(), scopus_count(), scopus_fetch(), scopus_trend(), scopus_compare_topics() and scopus_intersections() warn with scopus_warning_query_syntax for INDEXTERMS(), which pybliometrics documents as not working through the Search API.
  • scopus_top(by = "author") and as_bibliometrix() warn once per session (scopus_warning_first_author_only) that a set recorded as retrieved under STANDARD names first authors only. Sets retrieved by 0.4.0 record no view and do not warn.
  • An HTTP 429 marked QUOTA_EXCEEDED raises scopus_error_quota_exceeded, a subclass of scopus_error_rate_limit, and is not retried. scopus_abstract() and scopus_corpus() stop requesting at a spent quota and give the remaining identifiers their NA rows with one scopus_warning_quota_exceeded warning, where they tried each three times and warned for each.
  • The message for HTTP 403 no longer blames the quota, and a timeout raises scopus_error_timeout, a subclass of scopus_error_offline, with a message naming the time limit, where it said that the API could not be reached.
  • The script the app generates keeps each plan’s checkpoints in a directory of its own under scopus_cache_dir(), where plans shared one and overwrote each other’s checkpoints. A script generated now does not resume from the checkpoints of one generated by 0.4.0.
  • The script the app generates records the scopusflow version, notes when demo mode was on, saves the records before plotting, plots only where ggplot2 is installed and includes a comparison run with ‘Partition by year’ off, which it left out.
  • The app’s cost note for a topic comparison and the generated script’s comment on that cost give (terms + 1) × years requests, where they gave terms × years. The note’s advice to use fewer terms or years applies above 80 such requests.
  • scopus_diff_dois() orders its rows in byte order on every machine, where it followed the locale’s collation, and its printed line counts the records it could not compare for want of a DOI.
  • plot_scopus_comparison() writes each count in its labels without padding, where it padded the smaller counts to the width of the largest.
  • Inside a plan, the warning for a cell stopped at the offset ceiling advises scopus_fetch_plan(plan, cursor = TRUE), where it advised scopus_fetch(cursor = TRUE) or partitioning by year.
  • citation("scopusflow") gives the DOI that CRAN registered, https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.scopusflow, where it gave the Zenodo concept DOI, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21252669.

New features

  • scopus_fetch_plan() gains cursor, so a plan cell matching more than 5000 records can be retrieved whole and checkpointed. The default, cursor = FALSE, keeps offset paging, and a checkpoint serves only a request in its own paging mode.
  • scopus_fetch(), scopus_fetch_plan() and scopus_records() gain fields = "extended", adding the document type, source type, volume, issue, pages, ISSN, PubMed identifier, open-access status and, under COMPLETE, the abstract, at no extra quota.
  • summary() of a set retrieved with fields = "extended" counts its document types and reports how many records ‘Scopus’ labels errata or retracted, and the help explains why those labels do not screen a set for retractions.
  • With fields = "extended", as_ris() and as_bibtex() type conference papers, conference reviews, chapters and books by their ‘Scopus’ document type and add the volume, issue, pages, ISSN and, in RIS, the document type as M3. as_bibliometrix() adds DT, VL and IS.
  • scopus_abstract(include = "index_terms") returns the index keywords ‘Scopus’ assigns, in an idxterms column, under view = "FULL". scopus_corpus() gains keywords, to use them alone ("index") or with the author keywords ("both"). The default, "author", is unchanged.
  • write_scopus_corpus() writes, and as_theoryforge_corpus() returns, a scopus_corpus() result in theoryforge’s corpus schema, with a provenance block, keying cited works on the ‘Scopus’ identifier so that a work is one node however its DOI is written.
  • scopus_diff_records() compares two harvests record by record, matching records as scopus_combine(dedupe = TRUE) does. It gives each record’s citation counts in both and marks as conflict a record whose DOI the other harvest gives to a different record.
  • scopus_combine() gains dedupe = "id_or_doi", which also merges records with different identifiers that share a DOI, and accepts "id_or_shared_doi" as the name of the rule TRUE applies.

Minor improvements

  • scopus_corpus() reports its requests and the quota left in the n_requests and quota attributes, and records the search expression, when the search that found the records ran and the kind of keyword as query, retrieved_at and keywords.
  • scopus_fetch() and scopus_fetch_plan() record retrieved_until beside retrieved_at, their view as view and a finite cap as max_results. scopus_combine() records the latest of its inputs’ times as retrieved_until and keeps their view where they agree.
  • scopus_search_report() also returns the latest retrieval time as searched_until, the cap as max_results, the de-duplication rule as dedupe_rule and the number of DOIs that records with different identifiers share as doi_conflicts.
  • scopus_diff_dois() counts the records it could not compare for want of a DOI in the attributes n_old_without_doi and n_new_without_doi.
  • The app’s ‘Records’ tab says how many records the harvest holds and that its table shows the first 25, and its ‘Retrieval’ panel says when the cap stopped a cell. A failed harvest is reported with the message of the error that stopped it, without the wrapper that callr adds, marked ‘Scopus:’ when the package raised the error, as in the other panels.
  • The app’s ‘Top authors’ tab notes that a STANDARD harvest names first authors only.
  • In demo mode, the app’s live terminal says when a year lies outside the bundled corpus and which year it is drawn from, and the app notes under a topic comparison that its counts are illustrative.
  • The app’s status text has the contrast that text needs, its progress bar has an accessible name and value and each figure has a text alternative.

Fixes

  • scopus_plan(partition = "none"), scopus_count(), scopus_fetch() and scopus_intersections() read an empty years as no year limit, as they read NULL, where they stopped with an untyped error.
  • scopus_abstract() and scopus_corpus() read a reference list, or a cited work’s author list, that holds one item, where such a list stopped the batch with an untyped error. A keyword or reference list in any other shape they cannot read leaves that identifier an NA row and a warning, as an unreadable response already did, and the identifier is retried on resume.
  • Retry-After dates parse in any locale, where a German or French LC_TIME made every one NA.
  • A checkpoint that scopus_fetch_plan(), scopus_abstract() or scopus_corpus() fails to write, as on a full disk, gives a scopus_warning_cache_unwritable warning, and its records are kept, where they were lost to an error.
  • scopus_intersections() uses as given a concept that opens with a tag of scopus_field_tags() written with a space before the bracket, as the web interface writes TITLE-ABS-KEY ( x ), where it wrapped it in field again and the API refused it.
  • The app’s ‘Check size’ button shows any error in a notification, where an error that was not a scopus_error, such as the one a blank query raised, closed the session. ‘Check size’ and ‘Fetch records’ refuse a blank query with a notification.
  • Each app session keeps its checkpoints in a directory of its own, so closing one tab no longer deletes another’s mid-harvest.
  • Demo mode works when the app is launched as scopusflow::run_app() without attaching the package, where ‘Check size’ and ‘Fetch records’ failed.
  • The app’s size note clears when the search whose size it gave changes, where it stayed on screen for a different search. It writes counts in full, and ‘Check size’ refuses with a notification while a harvest runs.
  • The app’s export buttons appear once there is something to write, where a click with nothing to write failed without a message.
  • The app’s ‘By year’, ‘Top sources’ and ‘Top authors’ panels say when there is nothing to show, where they showed a plotting error, and a highlighted topic whose counts are all missing is drawn without the highlight. The live terminal of a demo harvest over every year no longer labels it with the year 0.

Documentation

  • The designing-queries article describes the offline query checks and gives a recipe for testing a strategy’s relative recall against records known to be relevant, following Sampson et al. (2006) and Bramer et al. (2018). It also explains loose and exact phrases and why a query mixing operators needs brackets.
  • The help for scopus_count(), scopus_fetch() and scopus_intersections() says that years is sent as one inclusive range, so c(2015, 2020) covers every year from 2015 to 2020, where it called them ‘publication years to restrict to’. ?scopus_compare_topics says that each year is counted on its own, where it called years a span.
  • The worked examples no longer present the bundled corpus as the result of an unquoted search. It came from an exact-phrase search in OpenAlex, and the demonstration plan and live searches quote the phrase, since ‘Scopus’ joins the words of an unquoted phrase with AND.
  • The help for scopus_compare_topics() and two articles give a topic comparison’s cost as (terms + 1) × years requests, where they gave one count request per term per year.
  • The app article no longer promises that a run stopped by the quota resumes in a later session, and points to the generated script for a harvest that has to continue after the session ends.
  • ?scopus_fetch_plan, ?scopus_cache_dir, the README and the articles give each plan a checkpoint directory of its own under scopus_cache_dir(), where they used scopus_cache_dir() itself, in which plans overwrite each other’s checkpoints.
  • The scopus_cache_clear() example points the cache at a temporary directory first, where running it deleted the managed cache.
  • The keywords-and-references article shows its calls without output and builds the shapes they return from example_records, where it printed invented keywords, references and quota.
  • The API access section of ?scopus_count names the condition class each HTTP status raises and documents the options scopusflow.max_tries and scopusflow.retry_backoff. The README says that, of the server errors, only 500, 502, 503 and 504 are retried, where it said that the whole 5xx range was.
  • The README writes the call for reference lists with view = "FULL", since scopus_abstract() refuses include = "references" under its default view.
  • The analysing-a-literature article and ?scopus_top say that a harvest under the default STANDARD view names the first author of each record alone, so an author tally counts first authorships, and that view = "COMPLETE" gives the author list, where they said that a live harvest returned every author.
  • ?scopus_combine says that c() on record sets calls scopus_combine(), so it renumbers them and keeps every row unless given dedupe, where it said that c() returned a list.
  • ?scopus_corpus says that records needs the identifier column that by names, ?summary.scopus_records that n_with_doi counts the records carrying a DOI and ?scopus_quota that reset is when the key’s quota resets. ?scopus_diff_dois no longer calls status an ordered factor.

scopusflow 0.4.0

CRAN release: 2026-08-21

A release about reporting a search and about trusting the cache. The package now writes a search up as the reproducible record a systematic review has to publish, and a family of silent cache defects that served the wrong records is fixed.

Writing up a search

  • scopus_search_report() assembles the reproducible search-strategy record a systematic review has to report, from a harvest or from a plan not yet run. It prints as a readable report, formats as a methods paragraph fit to paste into a manuscript (format(report, style = "paragraph")), and writes as Markdown when file is supplied. It carries the database and platform, the field-wrapped query of every cell, the year limits, view, page size and paging mode, the date searched, the records retrieved against the number the API reported as matching, per-cell completeness, duplicates removed, the software versions, a runnable snippet that rebuilds the plan, and an explicit map of which PRISMA-S items the package can supply and which only you can. The reporting standard is PRISMA-S (Rethlefsen et al., 2021, Systematic Reviews, 10, 39), with the identification counts of the PRISMA 2020 flow diagram.

    Because the output is written for a published methods section, the report states only what the objects record. An absent retrieval time is never replaced by the current one, a completeness figure is never given for a harvest whose reported total is unknown, duplicates are counted only where a merge recorded removing them, and every unverifiable field says it is unrecorded, in words. Ten of the sixteen PRISMA-S items, among them peer review of the strategy, grey literature and any other database searched, are listed as yours to supply, since the package has no evidence for them.

  • scopus_fetch_plan() now carries the per-cell accounting onto its result, as the cell_totals attribute, and sums it into total_results when (and only when) every cell reported a total. A cell that comes back shorter than the API said it should now warns, which the Python twin has done since 0.3.0, and the warning text is byte-identical between the two. A cell stopped by max_results is short by request and does not warn.

  • scopus_combine() records the merge in the combined attribute: how many records went in, how many were kept, how many were removed and whether de-duplication ran. That count exists only at the moment of the merge, and PRISMA-S asks for it.

  • A retrieval also records how it was paged, as the paging attribute, since an offset-paged query stops at the API’s ceiling where a cursor-paged one does not.

Cache defects that returned the wrong records

All were silent, and all are fixed.

  • A year-partitioned plan could be served another plan’s years, because checkpoints were keyed by the cell’s position alone and every cell of such a plan carries the same query (the year travels separately, as the API’s date parameter), so the guard meant to reject a foreign checkpoint could not tell 2015’s from 2016’s. A plan over 2016:2017 pointed at a cache written by a plan over 2015:2016 returned the 2015 records and reported “loaded from cache”. Checkpoints are now named cell-NNN-YYYY.rds and carry a manifest (query, date, view, page size and record cap) that resume compares against. Existing caches become invisible and refetch once, which spends a little quota to buy back correctness.
  • A cell cached under a max_results cap was served to a later request asking for more. The manifest now records the cap and whether it actually bit, so a truncated checkpoint is a miss for a wider request while an untruncated one stays usable for any request. The Shiny app’s cache key gained the record cap and now hashes the query, where it used to truncate it at 80 characters, so two long queries sharing a prefix no longer share a directory.
  • A zero-row checkpoint answered for any query. The guard that recognises a foreign checkpoint reads the cached rows’ query column, which an empty cell has no rows to carry, and the manifest comparison never consulted its own copy of the query, so a plan that legitimately found nothing left a checkpoint that a different plan pointed at the same cache_dir would load as its own empty result. The manifest’s query must now match as well.
  • A failed abstract retrieval was checkpointed as if it were data. A rate-limited, server-error or offline attempt in scopus_abstract() degrades to an all-NA row so the batch survives, but that row was written to the cache, so a resumed run read the failure back from disk and never retried it. Only rows parsed from successful responses are checkpointed now.
  • Two identifiers could share one abstract checkpoint, because the cache filename reduces every non-alphanumeric character to _, so distinct identifiers such as 10.1/a.b and 10.1/a-b collide on the same file, and resume never asked which identifier a cached row belonged to. The cached row’s own id must now match, and a collision warns and refetches.
  • A checkpoint holding more records than the current max_results asks for is now served trimmed to that cap, with the fuller set left on disk for a later, wider request. The opposite direction, a checkpoint truncated below what is asked for, already refetched with a warning.

A rejected or damaged checkpoint now warns, where it used to be mentioned only under verbose, and checkpoints are written to a sibling temporary file and renamed into place, so an interrupted run can no longer leave a half-written file that breaks every later resume.

Other fixes

  • scopus_combine() handed the merged set one input’s own retrieval attributes. rbind() keeps those of its first argument, so the result inherited that harvest’s plan, cell_totals and total_results even though it held the rows of several, contradicting the documented promise that per-retrieval attributes are not carried over. A search record read off the inherited total then called the union of two harvests complete against a figure belonging to one of them. Only what survives a merge is kept now: the earliest retrieval time, every contributing version, the paging mode where the inputs agree, and the merge counts themselves.
  • The PRISMA 2020 identification block counted the records identified after de-duplication, so the two figures it gives could not both be right: the diagram subtracts the duplicates removed from the records identified to reach the records screened, and 138 identified less 11 removed is not the 138 rows the set holds. Where a merge recorded how many records went into it, that is now the identification count.
  • A plan not yet run was described in the past tense, and its date line said the set did not carry a retrieval time, when the truth was that no retrieval had happened.
  • average_comparison_percentage summed the numerator over years the denominator excluded, so a year with a missing reference count inflated it, giving a figure that contradicted the per-year shares printed beside it and that drives the topic ordering in plot_scopus_comparison(). It is now computed over the years where both counts are available.
  • scopus_abstract(include = "references") aborted the whole batch when one document’s response omitted its reference-count attribute. Because that arrived as a bare base error, untyped and so outside the scopus_error hierarchy, the per-identifier handler could not catch it, defeating the documented promise that one bad identifier does not lose a batch.
  • The app’s demo banner still called the demo data synthetic, which was true of the six invented rows that shipped before 0.3.0. Demo mode has replayed 138 real published articles since then, and only the topic comparison is simulated, so the banner now says which is which.
  • A record count past 2^31 was coerced to NA at three points, each of which accepted any finite whole number and then reached for a 32-bit integer. scopus_top(n = ) left head.data.frame() raising an untyped error about its own argument; scopus_fetch(max_results = ) and scopus_fetch_plan(max_results = ) turned every later n >= max_results into NA, so the retrieval died on a bare “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”; and the app’s reproducible-code panel wrote max_results = NA into a script it promises is runnable. All three now carry the value as a double, so a cap wider than the result set simply never bites, which is what the Python twin has always done. A cap that fits stays an integer.
  • The 5000-record cap warning fired even when max_results had already asked for fewer records than the ceiling, advising a remedy for a problem the caller did not have.
  • scopus_compare_topics() carries its counts as doubles, matching scopus_trend() and scopus_intersections(), so billion-scale totals no longer coerce to NA.
  • Every request carries a 60-second transfer timeout, tunable through getOption("scopusflow.timeout"), so a stalled connection cannot hang a session.
  • Retrievals record when they were taken and by which package version, as the retrieved_at and scopusflow_version attributes, preserved through the .rds round trip. Both are attributes, so the documented schema and the CSV round trip are unchanged.
  • Every text file the package writes now carries LF line endings on all platforms: the BibTeX and RIS exports, the DOI and record CSVs, and the app’s script and comparison downloads previously arrived with CRLF endings when written on Windows.
  • Every print() method now sends its whole output to standard output. The header line went through cli, which writes to the message stream, so capture.output() returned the table without its header, and a knitted document showed one printed object as two separate blocks.

Continuous integration and metadata

  • The dependency canary could finish green having exercised nothing, when no development head was actually installed. It now says so, in a warning and in the step summary, and it installs the ggplot2 development head alongside the Imports.
  • The declared dependency floors are now installed and tested by a min-deps job, and the check matrix reaches back to roughly R 4.3.
  • rlang’s floor is corrected to 1.1.0. The evidence for it is httr2 1.0.0’s own DESCRIPTION, which requires rlang (>= 1.1.0), so the old floor described a combination no user could have installed. It is CRAN-visible metadata.
  • The documented request cost of the live API check, the cache guard’s description in the documentation and vignette, and the path to the Python twin’s copy of the example records were all corrected.

scopusflow 0.3.0

A data and documentation release. The bundled corpus becomes a real harvest, and every example and article is rebuilt on it.

The bundled example records

The dataset the package ships for offline work was replaced outright.

  • example_records is now a worked example harvest of 138 real journal articles on graphene supercapacitors published between 2015 and 2024, carrying their real titles, DOIs, source titles, first authors and citation counts. It replaces the six invented records shipped previously.
  • The records are not a ‘Scopus’ harvest and are not described as one. The Elsevier API terms do not permit redistributing retrieved records, so they come from OpenAlex, whose metadata is released under CC0, reshaped into the schema [scopus_fetch()] returns. The reasoning is recorded in the design notes.
  • The harvest is complete, so the rows per year are the real publications per year for that query. Eleven records carry no DOI and two no source title, kept as they arrive because a real harvest has such gaps.
  • scopus_id is empty throughout, these records not having come from ‘Scopus’, so de-duplication falls back to the DOI as it does for any record whose identifier is missing.

Documentation

The material a reader meets was rebuilt on the new corpus, and one misleading fixture was replaced.

  • Every vignette and example runs on that corpus, paired with the key-gated live call a reader would write, and the figures quoted in the prose were recomputed against the new data.
  • The demo mode of run_app() draws on the same corpus, so a first look at the app opens on real articles, where it used to show invented rows.
  • The parser fixture in inst/extdata moves onto the reserved 10.5555 example prefix. It previously paired genuine, resolving DOIs with invented titles and authors, so a reader who checked one found a real paper mislabelled.
  • Every vignette now turns console colour off and fixes the console width while it renders. pkgdown enables colour for its own build, and the escape sequences were reaching the reader as literal text in the middle of the tables.
  • vignette("comparing-topics") shows one year of its illustrative comparison across every topic, in place of the whole table, and leaves out the query column, which in a real comparison holds the whole query string and so reads badly in a table.
  • The README no longer opens with a link to the documentation site, which on the site’s own home page pointed the reader at the page in front of them.

scopusflow 0.2.1

A documentation release. The vignettes now demonstrate several features that 0.2.0 shipped but did not show.

  • vignette("designing-queries") shows the AND NOT operator in [scopus_query()], excluding a dominant homonym from a search.
  • vignette("analysing-a-literature") passes [scopus_intersections()] a concept that is already a complete field-tagged expression and so is used as given, letting a concept be a whole synonym set.
  • vignette("scopusflow") introduces [scopus_top()] on a record set, and points to the analysis article for the plots and trends built on it.
  • vignette("plans-and-quota") covers verbose = TRUE in [scopus_fetch_plan()], which reports a line as each cell is fetched or loaded from cache.
  • vignette("building-a-reference-set") shows [scopus_extract_dois()] on a plain vector of DOIs, both with the default deduplication (which ignores case and resolver prefixes) and with dedupe = FALSE.
  • vignette("keywords-and-references") tallies author keywords across a [scopus_corpus()] result, the per-keyword document count the article is named for.
  • [scopus_abstract()]’s help page no longer describes the Python twin’s reference fields.

scopusflow 0.2.0

This release reaches further into the API, adds an analysis and export layer on top of a retrieval, and introduces a local, code-free app.

Deeper retrieval

A search now reaches further into the API, past the offset ceiling and beyond the fields the Search endpoint returns.

  • [scopus_fetch()] gains cursor = TRUE, cursor-based pagination that retrieves a whole large query without the 5000-record ceiling of offset paging. The warning on a query that exceeds the ceiling suggests this alongside partitioning with [scopus_plan()].
  • [scopus_fetch()] and [scopus_fetch_plan()] add an authkeywords column when view = "COMPLETE" is requested, at no cost beyond that view’s own smaller page size. The view = "STANDARD" output is unchanged, and [read_scopus_records()] keeps the column across a CSV round-trip.
  • [scopus_abstract()] retrieves the abstract and fuller metadata for one or many records from the ‘Scopus’ Abstract Retrieval API, resilient to an identifier that cannot be found. Through view and include = c("references", "keywords") it also retrieves a document’s own reference list, as a structured, per-citation data frame, and author keywords, with per-identifier caching keyed by the requested view and extras, an n_requests/quota attribute, and a clear, actionable error on an entitlement 403 that stops the batch, so the same failure is not repeated for every identifier. include = "keywords" without view = "FULL" is rejected up front, since the REF response carries no author keywords.
  • [scopus_corpus()] combines a search result with abstract retrieval into a minimal id/title/year/keywords/references shape for downstream tools such as keyword co-occurrence or citation-network analysis, without replacing [as_bibliometrix()]. A new vignette, Author keywords and references, walks through all of this with real DOIs.
  • [scopus_fetch_plan()] compares each checkpoint’s recorded query with the plan cell before loading it, refetching and overwriting the checkpoint on a mismatch, so two different plans pointed at the same cache_dir cannot serve each other’s records. A checkpoint that carries no query information (a zero-row cell, or one written by scopusflow 0.1.0) loads as before, and a cache directory is still best kept to a single plan.

Analysis and plots

The package gains a layer for summarising a literature and drawing the result.

  • [scopus_trend()] reports annual record counts for a query (the size of a literature over time), with [plot_scopus_trend()].
  • [scopus_top()] tallies the most frequent sources or authors in a record set, with [plot_scopus_top()], which draws whole-number axis breaks (so a tally of small counts shows no fractional ticks) and derives the count axis’s headroom from the widest end-of-bar label (so a wide count, say five figures on a top-authors bar, does not clip at the panel edge). An autoplot() method draws a record set’s publications per year.
  • [scopus_intersections()] counts a named set of concepts and any requested intersections of them, sizing where a study or a niche sits within the surrounding literature at one count request per row. Concept values that are already complete field-tagged expressions are used exactly as given, with no second wrap. [plot_scopus_intersections()] draws the result as a lollipop chart on a log-scale axis, with an autoplot() method and an optional highlight (for example the niche itself) whose legend label is derived from what is highlighted: ‘Focal intersection’ for intersections, ‘Focal concept’ for concepts and ‘Focal set’ for a mixture. An explicit highlight_label still wins.
  • [plot_scopus_comparison()] gains legend_inside. When set, and a legend is drawn, it is placed inside the panel in whichever corner has the most free space, on a small semi-transparent background, where the default places it above the panel. That default is unchanged.
  • [plot_scopus_comparison()] now spreads the direct line labels vertically so topics that converge near the final year no longer overlap, and falls back to a legend when there are too many topics to label legibly. The labels are spread when the figure is drawn, against the rendered text height, so they stay legible at any figure size, including a short panel such as the app’s result card. They carry no leader lines. The labels are colour-matched to their lines and spread in the same order as the line ends, so the link is clear without a leader that would otherwise cut across neighbouring labels.

Export

A retrieval can now leave the package in the formats other tools read.

  • [as_bibtex()] and [as_ris()] export a record set to the BibTeX and RIS interchange formats, so a search can be carried into Zotero, EndNote, Mendeley or a LaTeX bibliography.

A code-free app

The whole workflow is now available without writing any R.

  • [run_app()] launches a local, code-free Shiny app for building a search, retrieving records with a live progress terminal, and exporting them. A panel mirrors every choice as a runnable R script, so the app is an on-ramp to the package. It runs on your own machine, so the API key never leaves it. The app also has a Compare topics tab (with highlight, stability-band and counts-in-label controls, a per-term progress indicator, a quota estimate and a CSV export) and a Demo mode, on by default, that synthesises records and a comparison so the whole workflow can be explored with no key and no network. A new vignette, Using the code-free app, walks through every panel.
  • The app holds steady under stress. It refuses to start a comparison while a harvest is running, turns any comparison failure into a notification, floors a fractional maximum-records entry, drops duplicate comparison terms, and tells you when there is nothing to cancel.

Other improvements

One rough edge in the package’s messaging was smoothed.

  • The no-key error renders its guidance (the option name, the api_key argument and the key-request URL) through cli, where it used to leak raw markup.

scopusflow 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-06-20

First release.

  • Reproducible search plans with [scopus_plan()], and cheap sizing with [scopus_count()].
  • Quota-aware, paginated retrieval through [scopus_fetch()], with the largest page each view allows requested by default to keep request counts low, and resumable, cached, partitioned retrieval through [scopus_fetch_plan()].
  • A stable normalised record schema from [scopus_records()], with a summary() method that gives a quick overview.
  • DOI extraction and change tracking with [scopus_extract_dois()] and [scopus_diff_dois()].
  • Topic-trend comparison with [scopus_compare_topics()], and a plot from [plot_scopus_comparison()] or autoplot().
  • Interoperability and I/O through [as_bibliometrix()], [write_scopus_records()] and [read_scopus_records()].
  • A reference to the common ‘Scopus’ field tags in [scopus_field_tags()], a safe query composer in [scopus_query()], and a bundled [example_records] dataset for offline exploration.
  • Safe merging of record sets with [scopus_combine()] (and a c() method), plus as_tibble() and as.data.frame() coercion.
  • A typed condition system (scopus_error and its subclasses) and quota-header parsing with [scopus_quota()].
  • The comparison plot uses whole-number year breaks, a colour-blind-safe palette, direct line labels, an optional highlight argument and a shaded Wilson stability band (an illustrative range, switchable with interval).
  • The bundled example_records spans several disciplines, and the examples and five workflow vignettes draw on a wide range of fields.
  • The authors column retains every author a record lists. Very large result totals are handled without overflow, and DOI cleaning copes with www.doi.org hosts and DOI: labels.
